opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: assume scalable correct variance already exists. Highest-yield hit is Limozin, Seaman, and Su (SMMR 2025; arXiv 2407.08317), co-authored with the TrialEmulation lead: they compare sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife, and a new LEF bootstrap for sequential trial emulation (STE) marginal risk differences under IPW. LEF is faster than full bootstrap and covers better under the sparse regimes that motivate STE; sandwich is fastest and covers well only with large n and medium/high event rates. They state explicitly that sandwich is the only CI method in TrialEmulation and that it ignores weight-estimation uncertainty. That is real progress on the sequential-eligibility half of the claim.

It does not close the problem as stated. Coverage guidance is setting-specific, not a single default. LEF is research code (GitHub simulation repo), not a TrialEmulation default. The design is parametric MSM/IPW STE, not nested clone-within-person-within-site dependence from multi-strategy cloning, and not influence functions for flexible nuisance models. Clone-censor-weight primers (Gaber et al. 2024; Webster-Clark et al. PDS 2025; survivalCCW) still recommend bootstrap or robust SE and ship bootstrap vignettes; they do not deliver streaming IF or Arrow/DuckDB risk-set variance. Queries run: sequential trial variance sandwich bootstrap jackknife; clone-censor-weight variance; TrialEmulation robust SE; arXiv 2407.08317; survivalCCW; Enders 2018 sandwich (still not off-the-shelf). No 2025–2026 package release supplies a general scalable correct default for both cloning and sequence expansion under flexible nuisances. Partial solve of STE inference guidance; core gap remains.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: assume causal evaluation of synthetic patients is already standard. The report's own prior work (Shi et al. 2022) already builds privacy-conscious synthetic data with ground-truth multi-treatment effects, so the agenda's proposed direction (causally annotated synthetic trials) has a published instance rather than a blank slate. Amad et al. (arXiv 2510.18768; NeurIPS 2025) explicitly diagnose evaluation on distributional resemblance while treatments invite causal analysis, state desiderata (covariate distribution, treatment assignment mechanism, outcome generation mechanism), propose metrics (precision/recall on covariates, propensity JSD, PEHE utility), and introduce STEAM to factor generation along that DGP. That is substantive prior art on evaluation design and generation, not mere marginal fidelity.

It does not solve the problem as a field practice claim. STEAM and Shi are proposals/datasets, not industry standard. Causal fidelity of a generator trained only on observational data remains non-identifiable without a structural gold standard; two SCMs can match all observational margins and disagree on interventions. Privacy mechanisms that erase rare strata still conflict with positivity-relevant tails. Hernandez et al. (Front Digit Health 2025) still frame synthetic tabular evaluation around fidelity/utility/privacy without interventional ground truth. Queries run: causal fidelity synthetic evaluation; STEAM treatment effect synthetic data; Shi 2022 ground truth; PEHE synthetic medical; synthetic patient counterfactual evaluation 2024–2026. No evidence that clinical or regulatory use treats synthetic-effect estimates as non-evidence by default, nor that mainstream generators are scored on intervention response error. Partial solve of evaluation methodology; the practice mismatch remains open.

resolving_work.quote: We produced a large-scale and realistic synthetic dataset that provides ground truth effects for over 10 hypertension treatments on blood pressure outcomes.

Partially closes the evaluation-design gap without making causal scoring universal practice.

opinions.rationale:
Inverted prior: assume executable code, versioned phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected protocols are already standard deliverables. TARGET (Cashin/Hansford et al., JAMA/BMJ 2025) is correctly scoped as a reporting checklist for protocol, mapping, estimands, assumptions, estimates, and sensitivity analyses; it is not a risk-of-bias instrument and does not require analysis code, code-list versions, weight diagnostics dumps, or failed protocol versions. That part of the claim stands.

Partial prior art exists in infrastructure, not in universal publication norms. OHDSI Phenotype Library is a public, version-controlled phenotype repository with release versioning and DOIs for cohort definitions (partial answer to phenotype logic and code-set versions, limited to OMOP/OHDSI contributors). Strategus/HADES encode analyses as shareable JSON-plus-R workflows on OMOP. THESEUS (Kim et al., medRxiv 2026.03.13.26348306) automates mapping free-text TTE descriptions to Strategus JSON and executable R, improving shareable machine-readable specs for OHDSI-style studies; it does not compel release of rejected protocols or non-OMOP phenotype licenses. Scattered tutorials (e.g. Hoffman steroids-trial-emulation with simulated data) and TrialEmulation show that reference code can be released, which does not make re-runnable artifacts common for applied emulations on licensed claims/EHR. Queries run: TARGET reproducibility code phenotype; OHDSI Phenotype Library; THESEUS Strategus TTE; STaRT-RWE HARPER code sharing; RECORD-PE STROBE rejected protocol versions. No 2025–2026 guidance requires publishing rejected protocol versions or institution-exportable simulated test datasets as the standard companion to TARGET. Legal and data-model barriers named in the problem remain. Partial solve for OHDSI-adjacent machine-readable design; field-wide unavailability of code, full phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected versions remains open.
